chart_check: Dual-axis bar+line chart, hours 0–23; left axis crashes in thousands (bars colored day blue / night orange per legend), right axis fatalities per 1,000 crashes (red line), annotation on the 4 am peak, source footnote. Bar heights and line points match values.csv (e.g., hour 16 ≈ 161k crashes, hour 4 ≈ 6.35 deaths/1,000); no cut-off or overlapping elements; crash total sums to 2,269,187 ≈ the stated n = 2.27M.
answer: Yes — daytime (7am–6pm) has the most crashes (~1.54M), but night crashes are far deadlier: 0.39 injuries/crash vs 0.30 by day, and ~28 fatalities per 10,000 night crashes vs ~10 by day; 4 am is the most dangerous hour, with ~6.4 deaths per 1,000 crashes, 8× the 4 pm rate.
